findings.title: The test writes the attack chars as literal non-ASCII characters instead of \u escapes
findings.description: "aĊb", "ačb" and "text/plainĊ" hold U+010A and U+010D as raw characters. They look almost the same as the ASCII letters C and c, so a reader cannot see which code point is under test, and an editor or tool that normalizes the text could quietly turn the case into ASCII. The build sets options.encoding = 'UTF-8', so it compiles correctly today. The point is readability and robustness, not correctness.

findings.title: SDS-AC-7 still says CR/LF only, but the test is tagged SDS-AC-7 and now covers chars above U+00FF
findings.description: The fix makes header() refuse more than before: any char above U+00FF. This is stricter than FR-HTTP-015 AC-4 and does not conflict with it, and docs/api/response.md and the HttpExchange javadoc were both updated. The SDS acceptance contract and its Test Plan row were not updated, so the SDS no longer matches the code. That matters at the SDS-to-code match gate and at kiwi-sds --close, where the refusal set should move into the SRS AC as a clarification.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend SDS-AC-7 and its Test Plan row to name 'a control char other than HTAB or a char above U+00FF', or note it for the --close step so it lands in FR-HTTP-015 AC-4.
